Definition: Extent to which the national digital identity system is integrated with the data exchange for identity verification and authentication
Comments: National Identification Card (CNI) is a multifunctional electronic smart card integrated with SNIAC (National System for Civil Identification and Authentication), PKI infrastructure, and the CMDCV (Mobile Digital Key). The system provides Single Sign On across government services and is integrated with PDEX data exchange layer. NOSi states goal to reach 100% resident adoption.
revision_notes: Original score of 5 (Fully Integrated) was not fully supported on re-check. SNIAC (Law 43/VIII/2013) is the authoritative civil identification system designed to feed subsystems (fiscal, electoral, border, social security, health, education) and CMDCV provides single sign-on authentication, but NOSi's own December 2025 National Governance Framework ToR describes a continuing 'silo landscape' with fragmented data-sharing and citizen-verification processes across ministries, and NOSi's 2024/2025 annual plans still list 'consolidating CMDCV' and reaching only 50% of residents with digital ID as in-progress objectives. Evidence supports substantial but not complete integration. Revised down to 4 (Partially integrated).
revised_comments: Cabo Verde's National Identification Card (CNI) and civil identification system (SNIAC), established under Law 43/VIII/2013, function as the authoritative source of identity data for other government subsystems, and the Mobile Digital Key (CMDCV) provides single sign-on authentication across public portals. Digital identity is one of NOSi's three strategic pillars and underpins authentication on the PDEX interoperability platform. Full integration across all sectoral systems remains a work in progress: the 2025 National Governance Framework for Digital Transformation notes continuing fragmentation and silos across ministry-run portals, and NOSi's annual plans still list consolidation of CMDCV and expansion of digital ID coverage as ongoing objectives.

Definition: Integration of court records, case management systems, correctional services data, legal aid information
Comments: Justice Information System (SIJ) restructured by NOSi to support electronic processing of court cases, eliminating paper use. Criminal Information System for online Criminal Record Certificate issuance by DGRNI. Integrated with government digital infrastructure.
revision_notes: Confirmed at 4 (Partially integrated), refreshed with newer evidence. The Justice Information System's criminal module (SIPP) has been operational since January 2025 and by March 2026 was reported complete and running in all judicial districts (comarcas); the civil module (SIPC) began implementation in April 2026. NOSi is the technical partner delivering the system, tying it into the wider government digital infrastructure. No evidence was found of integration of correctional services data or legal aid information, so full integration is not yet demonstrated.
revised_comments: The Justice Information System (SIJ), developed by NOSi for the Ministry of Justice, digitises court case processing. Its criminal-process module (SIPP) has been running since January 2025 and, as of March 2026, is fully operational across all judicial districts (comarcas), assigning a unique case number and enabling electronic case tracking for the Public Prosecution Service, Judicial Police and courts. A civil-process module (SIPC) began roll-out in April 2026. Management passes to the Institute for Justice Modernisation and Innovation (IMIJ) working alongside NOSi. Integration of correctional services and legal aid data into the exchange is not yet evidenced, so the system is best described as partially integrated with the wider data exchange.

Definition: Integration of passport issuance and immigration control data into the exchange platform
Comments: Electronic Passport (PEC) launched in Praia in 2016, meeting international requirements. Consular Portal (launched 2020) allows diaspora to apply for passports and ID cards online, integrated with SNIAC. Passport system connected through NOSi's interoperability infrastructure.
revision_notes: Confirmed at 5 (Fully Integrated), with fresher supporting evidence beyond the original 2016 launch date. The Automated Biometric Identification System at national borders (phase 2 completed 2022 at Sal airport, delivered with Zetes) verifies passport authenticity and passenger data at entry/exit points, and the Consular Portal integrates passport applications for the diaspora with SNIAC. This demonstrates passport issuance and immigration control data are tied together operationally.
revised_comments: Cabo Verde's electronic passport (PEC), introduced in 2016, is issued and managed through SNIAC, the national civil identification and authentication system. Passport data is used operationally at the border: the Automated Biometric Identification System, rolled out in phases and completed at Sal International Airport in 2022 (delivered with Zetes), verifies passport authenticity and biometric data against passenger records at entry and exit points. The Consular Portal, launched in 2020, allows the diaspora to apply for passports online through the same SNIAC-linked infrastructure. Passport issuance and immigration/border control are thereby integrated through Cabo Verde's identity and interoperability infrastructure.

Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: Cape Verde is Africa's data protection pioneer: Data Protection Law (Law 133/V/2001, amended 2013 and 2021). Law of Administrative Modernization updated to prioritize digital transactions. Law of System of Access and Reuse of Documents (2022). Legislative Decree No. 5/2020 on Mobile Digital Key. These collectively enable cross-government data sharing with regulatory framework.
revision_notes: Confirmed at 3 (Yes). Verified: Data Protection Law 133/V/2001 as amended by Law 41/VIII/2013 and Law 121/IX/2021 (DLA Piper); Law 43/VIII/2013 establishing SNIAC as the sole accredited system for citizen lifecycle data, with other public administration subsystems required to use its data (justica.gov.cv, sniac.cv); Legislative Decree 5/2020 establishing the CMDCV. These collectively provide primary legal authority for cross-government data sharing.
revised_comments: Cabo Verde has an established legal basis for cross-government data sharing. Law 43/VIII/2013 created the National System for Civil Identification and Authentication (SNIAC) as the sole accredited system for managing citizen lifecycle data, obliging other public administration subsystems (fiscal, electoral, border, social security, health, education) to draw on its records. This sits alongside the Data Protection Law (Law 133/V/2001, as amended by Law 41/VIII/2013 and Law 121/IX/2021) and Legislative Decree 5/2020, which establishes the Cabo Verde Mobile Digital Key (CMDCV) for authentication across public portals.

Definition: Current operational status of the data exchange system
Comments: PDEX (Platform for Data Exchange) is an operational interoperability/service bus platform developed and managed by NOSi since 2018. Per World Bank GovTech Maturity Index (2023): "In 2018, Cabo Verde launched the NOSI Cloud, a shared national cloud platform... together with the Data Exchange Platform (PDEX), which is a service bus extensively used by both central and local governments." Additional World Bank financing (2025) includes strengthening PDEX as a key activity. The system is described as partially operational; integration across all systems is ongoing.
revision_notes: Confirmed at 4 (Partially Operational). PDEX has been operational as a service bus since 2018 (World Bank GTMI 2022 update) and continues to be expanded under the 2025 World Bank Additional Financing to the Digital Cabo Verde Project, with NOSi's 2025 annual plan listing 'continuous improvement of PDEX' as an ongoing 2025 activity, indicating the platform is live but not yet at full maturity across all government systems.
revised_comments: The Platform for Data Exchange (PDEX), developed and operated by NOSi since 2018, functions as an interoperability service bus used by both central and local government entities in Cabo Verde. It continues to be strengthened under the World Bank-financed Digital Cabo Verde Project, with a 2025 Additional Financing package specifically targeting further development of PDEX and NOSi's 2025 workplan listing continuous improvement of the platform. The exchange is live and in active use but continues to expand its coverage across government systems, placing it at a partially operational stage.

Definition: Provisions ensuring national control over government data and protecting against unauthorized foreign access
Comments: NOSi is a government-owned entity (established 1998) hosting data in national data centers (NOSI Cloud). PKI infrastructure is nationally owned. Government Cloud platform managed by NOSi. Data Protection Law (2001, amended 2013/2021) requires prior authorization for international data transfers. Strong controls exist and enforced through national infrastructure.
revision_notes: Confirmed at 4 (Strong, enforced controls). NOSi, a state-owned entity, operates national data centres (NOSi Cloud) hosting government data domestically, and the Data Protection Law (amended 2021) requires authorisation for cross-border transfers of personal data, giving legal teeth to the sovereignty regime. Cabo Verde's own PKI already exists and underpins CMDCV authentication (confirmed in a 2023 ToR), and NOSi's 2025 workplan includes certifying its PKI to ISO-27001 and reinforcing cloud/network sovereignty. Some elements (a blockchain-based government cloud) are still being built, but core controls are established and enforced rather than merely on paper.
revised_comments: Cabo Verde exercises meaningful control over government data through NOSi, a state-owned entity that hosts government data in national data centres (NOSi Cloud) rather than relying solely on foreign infrastructure. The Data Protection Law (Law 133/V/2001, as amended in 2013 and 2021) requires authorisation for cross-border transfers of personal data, giving legal force to data sovereignty. The government operates its own Public Key Infrastructure underpinning the Mobile Digital Key (CMDCV), and NOSi's 2025 workplan includes ISO-27001 certification of its PKI and continued investment in sovereign cloud and network infrastructure, alongside a planned blockchain-based government cloud still under development.

Definition: Extent to which provincial/state and local governments participate in the data exchange
Comments: PDEX is described as "extensively used by both central and local governments." NOSi provides services to municipalities. The National Governance Framework ToR (2025) explicitly includes embassies and consulates in the scope. However, full participation across all islands/municipalities is unclear; some fragmentation noted.
revision_notes: Confirmed at 4 (Partial Participation). The World Bank's GovTech Maturity Index confirms PDEX is 'extensively used by both central and local governments.' The Municipal Information System (SIM/SIMple) is deployed in all municipalities for financial management, but advanced modules (territory/land management) are only live in a subset of municipalities (Sal, São Vicente, Praia, Maio, Boa Vista), with a 2025 World Bank-financed project under way to extend and modernise these municipal modules. This confirms partial, uneven sub-national participation rather than full participation.
revised_comments: Local governments participate in Cabo Verde's data exchange, but coverage is uneven. The Platform for Data Exchange (PDEX) is used by both central and local government bodies. The Municipal Information System (SIM), covering core financial management, is operational in all municipalities, but more advanced modules such as land/territory management (SIM LAND/SIMple) are so far only deployed in a handful of municipalities (Sal, São Vicente, Praia, Maio and Boa Vista). A World Bank-financed technical assistance project is under way to develop and roll out further SIMple territory-management modules nationwide, indicating sub-national participation is still expanding rather than complete.
